issues.description: AlterTable restructuring removes ability to chain multiple operations in one ALTER TABLE
issues.detail: The previous grammar wrapped the OneOf inside Delimited(), allowing comma-separated mixed operations (e.g., ADD ... , DROP COLUMN ...). The new grammar replaces Delimited(OneOf(...)) with bare OneOf(...), so a single ALTER TABLE can now contain only one top-level clause. The removed test case (ADD column_b ... , DROP COLUMN column_a, DROP COLUMN IF EXISTS column_c) is valid T-SQL per MS docs and now fails to parse. This is a regression masquerading as a cleanup.

issues.description: DEFAULT_LANGUAGE allowing NumericLiteralSegment is not documented as supported
issues.detail: The CREATE LOGIN grammar now accepts a numeric literal for DEFAULT_LANGUAGE. MS docs specify a language name/alias (sysname). No test covers the numeric form, and adding a permissive branch without justification or fixture risks accepting invalid SQL silently. Either drop the NumericLiteralSegment branch or add a fixture demonstrating the documented use case.

issues.description: Identity seed/increment grammar accepts signed increment but tests only cover signed seed
issues.detail: SignedSegmentGrammar is added before both numeric literals in IdentityGrammar. While negative seed is valid, a negative increment is uncommon. The added fixture only tests IDENTITY(-2147483648, 1). Consider a fixture for the increment side, or restrict the optional sign to the seed only if increment cannot be negative per spec.

issues.description: DROP CONSTRAINT IF EXISTS parsed inconsistently across delimited items
issues.detail: The new DROP CONSTRAINT grammar makes the inner 'CONSTRAINT [IF EXISTS]' sequence optional, meaning subsequent items in the delimited list may omit the CONSTRAINT keyword entirely (just an ObjectReferenceSegment). T-SQL requires CONSTRAINT before each name in a delimited list. This may accept invalid SQL like 'DROP CONSTRAINT a, b'. Consider making the CONSTRAINT keyword required per item.

issues.description: Removed example was actually valid T-SQL per Microsoft documentation
issues.detail: The deleted line 'ALTER TABLE dbo.doc_exc ADD column_b ... CONSTRAINT exb_unique UNIQUE, DROP COLUMN column_a, DROP COLUMN IF EXISTS column_c' is copied verbatim from MS docs for sp_help. Calling it 'invalid' in the PR description and removing it reduces real coverage. If the restructure breaks it, the restructure is the bug, not the fixture.

review.summary: The PR adds useful T-SQL parser support (table var indexes, CREATE LOGIN options, negative identity seed, delimited DROP COLUMN/CONSTRAINT) with fixtures, but the AlterTable restructuring drops the outer Delimited() that previously allowed multiple mixed ALTER operations in one statement. The removed test fixture was actually valid T-SQL per Microsoft docs, so this is a regression presented as a cleanup. Smaller concerns: DEFAULT_LANGUAGE numeric branch is undocumented/untested, the DROP CONSTRAINT inner-optional sequence may accept malformed lists, and the signed identity grammar is only tested on the seed.
